Subject: Re: Pricing and billing for scoring-heavy workflows

Samir — thanks for the note and projection. High level answers below; I'll follow up with a short worked example and propose a pilot credit.

How scoring is billed (hosted API, default):
- Scoring unit: each candidate scored by a reranker/classifier counts as one scoring unit. For a rerank call with N candidates we bill N scoring units.
- Token component: when the request includes generated candidate context or when the model generates text (e.g., classifier explanations), model tokens are billed separately at our per-token generation rate.
- Minimums/rounding: we round scoring units to the nearest whole unit per request; streaming/partial scores still count per item scored.

Baseline pricing (hosted, public rate card):
- Scoring unit: $0.012 / scored item (per 1 scoring unit)
- Generation tokens: $0.0004 / token (for generated explanations/metadata)

Worked example (your projection, ballpark):
- 100M queries/month x 40 candidates = 4,000M scored items/month -> 4,000M x $0.012 = $48,000/month before discounts.
- If you also generate explanations averaging 5 tokens per scored item: 4,000M x 5 x $0.0004 = $8,000/month.
- Combined (baseline hosted): ~$56,000/month.

Discounting/packaging (typical starting point):
- Pilot: 10–20% credit for a limited pilot (we usually do a $10k–$25k credit depending on scope).
- Committed tiers: 10% off for 3-month pilot commitment; 18–25% for 12-months at larger minimum ARR; additional contract negotiation available for enterprise terms.

Two quick notes: dedicated capacity (Reserved/Dedicated) can change the math (lower per-unit rates but requires commit) and we can add an overage cap for predictability.

I'll loop in our pricing lead and proposals team for a formal rate card and SOW. Are you available tomorrow morning for a 30-min walkthrough?

— Markus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing and billing for scoring-heavy workflows — recommended tiers and language

Markus / Aditya — forwarding Samir's questions and Olive's projection. Suggested commercial language and math below for the proposal. Please review and OK to send to Samir.

Summary assumptions (use for the quote):
- Olive projection: 100M queries / month with 40 candidates avg -> 4,000M scoring units/month.
- Baseline hosted rate used for modeling: $0.012 / scoring unit + $0.0004 / generation token.

Recommended tiered pricing (hosted API):
- Pilot (0–3 months): 20% pilot credit applied to usage up to $25,000 (one-time, applied in invoice).
- Commitment A (6 months): 10% discount off baseline for committed monthly usage >= $25k/month; 15% discount for >= $50k/month.
- Commitment B (12 months): 20% discount for monthly commit >= $30k; 25% for >= $75k.

Suggested dedicated/reserved delta (optional):
- Offer a reserved pricing model that reduces scoring unit price by ~35–45% compared to hosted public rates for customers that commit to reserved capacity. Example: $0.012 -> $0.0075 (approx 37% reduction) with a 12mo commit and minimum $X/month. Final number to be set by Capacity team + Ops.

Billing definition to include in SOW (precise language):
- "Scoring unit" is defined as each candidate submitted to a Redwood rerank or classifier endpoint that is evaluated by the model. If a request includes N candidates, the request counts as N scoring units.
- Token billing for any generated content (including classifier explanations) is billed separately at standard per-token rates.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching reduces compute and latency but does not change the counting of the scoring unit. We can grant caching-based credits in exceptional pilots (term sheet).

Sample cost math (for procurement):
- Baseline hosted: 4,000M scoring units x $0.012 = $48,000/mo
- After 20% discount (12mo commit example): $48,000 * 0.8 = $38,400/mo
- + token charge (if applicable) ~= $8,000/mo -> total ~$46,400/mo effective cost

Commercial protections & asks:
- Rate card valid for 60 days from proposal date.
- Overage cap option: we can add a monthly percent cap on overruns to protect procurement (to be negotiated).
- Include a clause for periodic review if real usage deviates >30% from projection.

Recommended next steps:
1) Finalize draft SOW & pricing table (I can prepare).
2) Share pilot credit amount ($15k recommended unless you want to go to $25k for faster close).
3) Schedule internal capacity call to firm reserved pricing if Olive prefers dedicated.

If you approve, I'll attach a short SOW draft and the price table and send to Samir with a 30-min walkthrough.

– Marissa
